title: Firm-reported AI effects remain limited in retrospect but expand in expectation
geography: United States, United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia

observations.period: 2026; executive firm survey covering prior three years and next three years

denominator.unit: senior business executives (nearly 6000) at firms in the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia

no_past_three_year_firm_employment_or_pr.unit: percent of executives reporting no impact

expected_next_three_year_productivity_ch.unit: percent average expected increase at own firm

expected_next_three_year_output_change.unit: percent average expected increase at own firm

expected_next_three_year_employment_chan.unit: percent average expected change at own firm
percent average expected change at own firm

observations.method: Executive survey reported in NBER Working Paper 34836, with firm AI use, retrospective own-firm effects, and forward expectations measured in a common instrument; the survey covers firms in four countries.
observations.uncertainty: The source reports executive perceptions and expectations, not linked administrative outcomes or a randomized firm treatment. The four-country sample is not a US-only estimate, expected changes may not be realized, and the page does not by itself identify occupation, worker subgroup, implementation rule, pay, hours, or bargaining effects.
observations.subgroup: Younger and more productive firms report higher usage; employer and employee expectations are compared as distinct respondent perspectives.
observations.counterinterpretation: A gap between employer and employee expectations can reflect different information, incentives, or definitions of employment rather than a realized conflict. Low retrospective impact can coexist with impending reorganization, and expected productivity gains need not reach workers or households.

boundary: This is a firm-expectations layer for the AI-at-work program. It distinguishes current adoption, low reported retrospective effects, and expected future productivity/output/employment changes. It does not establish realized employment loss, worker control, pay, household security, cultural meaning, political response, or geopolitical power, and it must not be pooled with worker-level telemetry without a common unit and period.
